text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Russian foreign ministry legal and human rights experts are visiting Estonia to study the situation of the Russian-speaking population, which makes up around one third of the country.
- German navy commander Vice-Admiral Hans Boehmer is on a visit to Estonia and met the defence minister, defence forces commander and naval staff.

- European Affairs Minister Andra Veidemann took her oath of office and described her main task as making legislation conform to EU standards, lobbying EU states for early Estonian entry and a national debate on EU membership.
- The right-wing Fatherland Union wants to impose lower excise duty on domestically-produced beer. The Reform Party accuses it of protecting its backers' interests.
- Schoolteachers oppose the current system of wages as they say it reduces income and increases the workload.

- Estonia's leading university, Tartu University, expelled three students for computer hacking. They had illegally accessed a Taiwanese bank network and violated users' rules in the university network.
- The privatisation agency is to sell 32.9 percent of the Eesti Tubakas tobacco firm. Swedish firm and current main shareholder Svenska Tobaks has first refusal.
